questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Image of a Line Segment Under the Action of a Linear Transformation
questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

A line segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ has endpoints at $A(1,-2)$ and $B(-2,1).$ What are the coordinates of the corresponding endpoints of $\overset{―}{{A}^{′}{B}^{′}}$, the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the endpoints of $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective endpoints of the image are ${A}^{′}(-1,-4)$ and ${B}^{′}(-1,-1).$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}].

A line segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ has endpoints at $A(1,1)$ and $B(-1,2).$ What are the coordinates of the corresponding endpoints of $\overset{―}{{A}^{′}{B}^{′}}$, the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of $\overset{―}{AB}$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the endpoints of $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 2 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective endpoints of the image are ${A}^{′}(2,2)$ and ${B}^{′}(-5,7).$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

A line segment $\overset{―}{KL}$ has endpoints at $K(1,0)$ and $L(0,2).$ What are the coordinates of the corresponding endpoints $\overset{―}{{K}^{′}{L}^{′}}$, the image of $\overset{―}{KL}$ under the action of $T?$

${K}^{′}($

questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of $\overset{―}{KL}$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the endpoints of $\overset{―}{KL}:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 0 & 2\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot 2 \\ 3\cdot 1+1\cdot 0 & 3\cdot 0+1\cdot 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective endpoints of the image are ${K}^{′}(2,3)$ and ${L}^{′}(-2,2).$

questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $GHI$ has vertices at $G(5,5),\,H(-1,-4),$ and $I(3,5).$ What are the coordinates of the corresponding vertices of  $△{G}^{′}{H}^{′}{I}^{′}$, the image of $△GHI$ under the action of $T?$

${G}^{′}($ 
{{field-1}}, 
{{field-2}}
$),\,$  $\,{H}^{′}($ 
{{field-3}}, 
{{field-4}}
$),\,$ $\,{I}^{′}($ 
{{field-5}}, 
{{field-6}}
$)$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of $△GHI$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $GHI:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 & 3 \\ 5 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 & -1 & 3 \\ 5 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-15 & 15 & -17 \\ 25 & -14 & 21\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of $△{G}^{′}{H}^{′}{I}^{′}$ are ${G}^{′}(-15,25),$
${H}^{′}(15,-14),$ ${I}^{′}(-17,21).$

questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-2,1),(3,3),$ and $(5,-2).$ Which of the following are coordinates of a vertex of ${S}^{′}$, the image of $S$ under the action of $T?$

- $(5,-2)$
- $(-2,-5)$
- $(3,12)$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of $S$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 & 5 \\ -5 & 12 & 13\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(-2,-5),(3,12),(5,13).$ 

So, the correct answer is "II and III only."

$$
